meaning: Carcharhinus, from Greek karcharias “a kind of shark” (from karcharos “saw-like, jagged”, for its teeth) + rhinus, an ancient word for sharks; galapagensis, Latin for “from the Galápagos”, the type locality
description: A large, slender brownish-grey shark with a broadly rounded snout, large sickle-shaped pectoral fins, a moderately tall first dorsal fin and a low ridge between the two dorsals. It is common around remote oceanic islands, where it patrols reefs and slopes and eats mostly bottom-living fish and octopus. Young sharks stay in shallow water, away from the larger adults that may eat them.
eats: Bottom-living fish, octopus and squid, rays and smaller sharks
